doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Don't imitate: fingerprints, and being a sideman
summary: He tells students they can never sound like anyone else, then reflects that he was a sideman all his life, as the title of his book says.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well you said an interesting thing before, they ask you well how did you do it, and you say well don’t do what I did. But let’s talk about what you did.

All right. Well the reason I give them, they say well you know like you say listen to Lester or Charlie or one of them guys. They says but that would be imitating. I says you can never imitate the same. Because they says what do you mean, we could play it. I says you see that? What am I showing you?
Yeah. And a fingerprint. Every one of us has got a different fingerprint see. So I tell them that. So don’t be afraid, you ain’t going to sound like them.
Even if you try you’re not going to.
Even if you try. See and one time when I was, well you know I did a lot of different kinds of things. I was in big time but I wrote a book you know.

Sideman. Well that’s what I probably was all my life. You know, even if I was the leader I was still, when I led the group it was like, you know, if Clark Terry was there, he’d be the leader for that night. Well anyway, what was I saying?
